newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends mixed after British budget roils market.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends mixed after British budget roils market.

text.p: The dollar ended mixed after Britain's budget boosted sterling and an announcement of big losses at Switzerland's largest bank lifted the dollar against the Swiss franc.
British officials unveiled a 1997 budget with a 1 percent income tax cut and forecasts for strong economic growth in coming years.
That positive forecast convinced some investors that British interest rates may continue to rise, prompting sterling buying.

"People bought the British pound immediately because they perceived the budget to be a good one," said James Powers, vice president for corporate foreign exchange at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale in New York.
The pound rose to $1.6750 before slipping back to $1.6717 late Tuesday, up from $1.6683 in late Monday trade.
Sterling also rose against the German mark, helping the dollar rise against the mark as well.
But after brushing 1.53 marks, the dollar slipped back to 1.5244 late in the session, a touch higher than Monday's close at 1.5236.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp told a conference in Hamburg that any delay in the proposed single European currency would bolster the mark, prompting mark buying, dealers said.
"We heard talk of large corporate selling of dollars near 1.53 marks after the Krupp comments," said Russel Lascala, chief spot currency trader at Citibank.
The dollar dipped to 112.50 Japanese yen from 112.63 late Monday, but rose to 1.2905 Swiss francs from 1.2885.
The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3427 from C$1.3430.

The Swiss franc came under pressure early in the session after a report that Union Bank of Switzerland would take a $2.3 billion charge to cover expected bad loans as a result of weak Swiss economic growth.
The dollar hit a fresh 21-month high at 1.2964 Swiss francs on the news, which hinted at a prolonged Swiss slump.
"The Swiss domestic economy is weak and that fuelled dollar buying against the franc. You can't ignore the reason why UBS is doing this," Powers said.
Against the yen, the dollar traded in a narrow range as investors awaited the latest Japanese business sentiment survey, or Tankan report, due Wednesday.
Japan's economy has suffered through an extended slump and currency dealers said the yen could rally on any surprising news of strength in the report.
"Things could get pretty wild Wednesday after the Tankan. The risk is on the downside for the dollar," Lascala.
An intraday slump in U.S. stock prices helped restrain the dollar, dealers said.
After climbing to a new record on Monday, stock prices tumbled Tuesday, prompting some investors to take profits from dollar holdings, dealers said.
Dealers said currency trading is expected to wind down early Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday.
